Feature.Description:
Workflow-level control of an Opentrons Flex.
Commands *do* something to the robot; anything that merely reads state is a Property, so a client can read it without asking the robot to act.
A command here is one deliberate action an operator would ask for: move this labware, shake this module, open this latch. A whole procedure is a recipe, run by ExecuteRecipe. There is deliberately no general "run these steps inline" escape hatch: it duplicated the recipe format inside a workflow parameter, gave the caller no validation and no checking against the deck, and was harder to use than the recipe file it replaced.
Commands whose description begins with MOVES HARDWARE physically move the robot. Everything else is safe to call at any time.

Property.Description: Current robot state as JSON: state, run_id, connected, config. Replaces the former GetStatus command — reading state is not an operation, and as a Property it can be polled or subscribed to without appearing in the command list as something to "run".
Id of the protocol run in progress, or empty when idle.
The HAL configuration currently loaded, as JSON ({name, config}). This is what ExecuteRecipe runs against.
Per-rack tip consumption as JSON: load name, slot, used, available.
Robot metadata as JSON: name, model, serial, firmware version.

Whether the robot's camera is on, and where to watch it, as JSON: cameraEnabled, liveStreamEnabled, errorRecoveryCameraEnabled, and the hls and rtmp stream URLs.
The Flex has a native camera API - a still photograph, and an HLS/RTMP live stream - and all three enablement flags ship off. With them off every capture comes back "Cannot take photo, camera is disabled", which reads like a broken endpoint rather than a setting. SetCameraEnabled turns it on.
Attached modules (heater-shaker, temperature module) as a JSON array.

Command.Description: MOVES HARDWARE. Home all robot axes to their default positions.
MOVES HARDWARE. Stop the current run, force-drop any tips, and home. Never reports success if the drop/home sequence itself failed — read the response text before assuming the deck is safe.

Response.Description: What was actually stopped, dropped and homed.

Command.Description: Turn the deck lights on or off.

Parameter.Description: True to switch the lights on.

Command.Description: Switch the active HAL configuration. Persists to Library/HardwareConfig/.active, so it survives a server restart. Recipes are not paired with a HAL: set it once, and every later ExecuteRecipe runs against whatever is active.

Parameter.Description: File name in Library/HardwareConfig.

Command.Description: MOVES HARDWARE. Run a saved recipe against the currently active HAL configuration. Fails loudly if the run's own final state is anything other than "succeeded" — a stopped or errored run is not a success.

Parameter.Description: File name in Library/Recipes.

Response.Description: The robot's own run id, for looking the run up later.

Command.Description: Check a recipe against the active HAL configuration without running it: every labware the recipe requires must be present on the deck, and the generated protocol must compile. Safe to call at any time.

Parameter.Description: File name in Library/Recipes.

Command.Description: MOVES HARDWARE. Resume a paused protocol.
MOVES HARDWARE. Abort the running protocol. Drops tips first when safety.auto_drop_tip_on_abort is set.

Response.Description: Status message; warns explicitly if the tip drop failed.

Command.Description: MOVES HARDWARE. Move a piece of labware to another deck slot using the gripper. Implemented for a long time but not reachable: moving a plate between slots required authoring a whole recipe file.

Parameter.Description: Logical name from the active HAL config (e.g. MyPlate).
Destination deck slot (e.g. C2), or a module's logical name.
True to move with the gripper; false pauses for a manual move.

Command.Description:
MOVES HARDWARE. Set a heater-shaker or temperature module's target temperature. Set Celsius to 0 to deactivate heating.
MOVES HARDWARE means the module actuates - the latch, the shaker, the heater. The robot arm does not move and does not home: this goes straight to the module, outside any protocol run, and returns in milliseconds. Run it while a protocol is running only if you know what that protocol is doing.
The module must be declared in the active hardware config AND reported attached by the robot. If it is not, the command fails immediately and nothing actuates.

Parameter.Description: Logical module name from the active hardware config, or the module type. Checked against the config and against what the robot reports attached before anything moves.
Target temperature in degrees Celsius; 0 deactivates.
Block until the target is reached.

Command.Description:
MOVES HARDWARE. Shake a heater-shaker for a set time. The latch must be closed; set DurationSeconds to 0 to stop shaking immediately.
MOVES HARDWARE means the module actuates - the latch, the shaker, the heater. The robot arm does not move and does not home: this goes straight to the module, outside any protocol run, and returns in milliseconds. Run it while a protocol is running only if you know what that protocol is doing.
The module must be declared in the active hardware config AND reported attached by the robot. If it is not, the command fails immediately and nothing actuates.

Parameter.Description: Logical module name from the active hardware config, or the module type. Checked against the config and against what the robot reports attached before anything moves.
Shake speed in revolutions per minute.
How long to shake; 0 stops shaking.

Command.Description:
MOVES HARDWARE. Open or close a heater-shaker's labware latch. It must be closed before shaking and open before the gripper can place or remove a plate.
MOVES HARDWARE means the module actuates - the latch, the shaker, the heater. The robot arm does not move and does not home: this goes straight to the module, outside any protocol run, and returns in milliseconds. Run it while a protocol is running only if you know what that protocol is doing.
The module must be declared in the active hardware config AND reported attached by the robot. If it is not, the command fails immediately and nothing actuates.

Parameter.Description: Logical module name from the active hardware config, or the module type. Checked against the config and against what the robot reports attached before anything moves.
True to open the latch, false to close it.

Command.Description: Record that a tip rack has been physically refilled.

Parameter.Description: Deck slot of the refilled rack (e.g. A1), or "all".

Command.Description: Reset every tip-consumption counter to full.

Turn the robot's camera and live stream on or off. Nothing moves.
This is a setting on the robot, not on this server: it persists across a restart of either, and it ships off. It is the reason a capture can fail without the camera ever being asked for a frame.
Leaves the error-recovery camera setting alone - whether the robot films its own error recovery is a separate decision.

Parameter.Description: Enable the camera for stills.
Enable the HLS/RTMP live stream. Read its URLs from the CameraStatus property.

Response.Description: The resulting camera state, same shape as CameraStatus.

Command.Description:
Photograph the deck with the robot's on-board camera and save the image under Results/Images, where the web interface serves it.
Two acquisition paths are tried. First the robot's HTTP camera endpoint, which takes a picture without moving anything. If that is unavailable, capture falls back to running a one-step protocol on the robot — and starting a protocol HOMES THE ROBOT, so the fallback is refused unless AllowRobotMotion is true. The response always says which path was used and why the other was not.

Parameter.Description: Short name for the image file. Optional.
Permit the protocol-based fallback, which homes the robot. Leave false unless someone is watching the deck.
